title: Frequency Counter
story: The election results are in: a Vec of votes — "Alice", "Bob", "Alice", "Carol", "Alice", "Bob". Who won? You can't just look at the Vec — you need to count how many times each name appears. Time to tally the votes with a frequency counter!
why: Frequency counting with a Map is the core pattern behind vote tallies, word clouds, log analysis, recommendation engines, and any system that asks 'how often does X appear?'
analogy: A frequency counter is like tally marks on a whiteboard — every time someone votes for Alice, you add a mark under her name. At the end, the name with the most marks wins. The Map IS the whiteboard.
try_it: Count character frequencies in a string: convert a Str to a Vec[Str] of single characters (use string operations), then count frequencies. Find which letter appears most. Then build a 'majority vote detector' — returns true if any item appears more than 50% of the time. Add a tie-breaker: if two items have the same max frequency, return the one that appears first in the Vec.
tips: The increment pattern: `get->default(0)->+1->insert` — do this for every item in the input
Finding max/min requires a separate scan — you can't know the winner until all votes are counted
Use `contains` or `get` with a None default — both work, but `get` + default avoids a second lookup
common_mistakes: Forgetting to handle first occurrence — the initial `get` returns None, so default to 0
Using `counts.insert(item, counts.get(&item) + 1)` — `.get` returns Option, you can't + 1 on it
Scanning the Map for max without a known key list — you need a Vec of candidates to iterate
